- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.6) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.3) — model fails to recognize bearish momentum or mean reversion.
- Lag in downward corrections: model often delays price drops, especially after sentiment shifts to negative or neutral.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights recent lows — correct by smoothing out extreme deviations from 30-day moving average.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to short-term sentiment swings — dampen forecast volatility when sentiment is volatile or near zero.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — sentiment history should be averaged over 3–5 days for robust trend alignment.
